h1: What permits and zoning rules apply to finishing an attic in Newton, MA?
title: Newton Attic Conversion Rules: Building Permits, Height and Floor Area
description: Understand building-code review and Newton's zoning definition of a half-story before converting an attic into living space.
short_answer: Converting an attic into living space is a building alteration that should be reviewed by Newton ISD. Newton zoning also defines a half-story by the amount of floor area with a ceiling height of at least 7 feet under a sloping roof. The project's height, floor area, and building-code compliance must be checked against the actual plans.

facts.text: The state building code requires a permit before regulated alterations to a building.
Newton defines a half-story under a sloping roof as a story where the area with a ceiling height of 7 feet or more is less than two-thirds of the area of the story below.

qa.q: Does finishing an existing attic automatically count as a new full story?
qa.a: Not automatically. Newton's half-story definition uses the qualifying ceiling-height area under a sloping roof. The result depends on the actual floor plan and roof section.
